Test Case Title: Invoicing Delete requires Manage AP/AR (AP/AR gate)
Preconditions: Logged in as an Admin who can create custom roles. On the Roles & Permissions screen.
Steps to Reproduce (Manual):
1. Go to Administration → Roles & Permissions → click "Create Custom Role".
2. In the template picker, click "Skip" (start blank).
3. In the Permissions tree, turn "See Financial Data" ON, and make sure "View and Manage AP/AR Data" is OFF.
4. Under "Invoicing & payments", enable "Delete / Reverse".
5. Watch what the toggle does to its dependencies.
Expected Result: Enabling Invoicing "Delete / Reverse" should require BOTH "See Financial Data" AND "View and Manage AP/AR Data". With AP/AR OFF, the app should prompt to enable "View and Manage AP/AR Data" (a dependency confirmation, like the "Enable See Financial Data?" prompt) — or otherwise block/auto-enable it — so the role cannot hold Delete/Reverse without AP/AR access.
Actual Result (Observed): Enabling "Delete / Reverse" auto-checked Invoicing View + Create & Edit and (where relevant) the See-Financial-Data gate behaved, BUT NO "View and Manage AP/AR Data" prompt/gate fired at all — AP/AR stayed unchecked and the role saved with Delete/Reverse but without AP/AR access. The AP/AR dependency is not enforced.
Reason for Failure (Root Cause): The AP/AR-Data dependency gate is not wired for the Invoicing "Delete / Reverse" permission. Only the "See Financial Data" dependency is implemented; the parallel "View and Manage AP/AR Data" dependency is missing, so a role can be granted invoice Delete/Reverse without the AP/AR data permission the spec requires. (Financial gate works; AP/AR gate absent.)
Severity: Medium (permission-integrity gap — role can under-scope AP/AR while holding a destructive invoice action).

Test Case Title: Time Clock - A. View inspections on a work order line
Feature / Area: Custom Roles → Digital Inspections (Time Clock role access)
Preconditions: A user assigned the system "Time Clock" role. Digital Inspections feature enabled on the org.
Steps to Reproduce (Manual):
1. As Admin, assign a test user the "Time Clock" role.
2. Log out and log back in as that Time Clock user (fresh login so permissions load).
3. Look at the left navigation and try to open Work Orders / view an inspection on a work order.
Expected Result: A Time Clock user has clock-in/out only and NO Work Orders access, so they cannot open work orders or view Digital Inspections.
Actual Result (Observed): The Time Clock user CAN access Work Orders — the live "Time Clock" role includes the "workOrdersView" permission, so the Work Orders list renders and inspections on a WO are viewable (read-only). This contradicts the "no Work Orders access" expectation.
Reason for Failure (Root Cause): Role-template configuration drift. The "Time Clock" system role in this build grants workOrdersView (plus scheduleView, timesheetsView), whereas the test spec assumes Time Clock = clock-in/out only. Because Work Orders is accessible, Digital Inspections on a WO are reachable — so the test's "no access" expectation cannot hold with the current Time Clock role definition.
Severity: Medium (spec-vs-build drift on a system role; decide whether Time Clock SHOULD include workOrdersView, then fix the role or the spec).

Test Case Title: Time Clock - G. Inspection status labels display correctly
Feature / Area: Custom Roles → Digital Inspections (Time Clock role — status labels)
Steps to Reproduce (Manual):
1. As Admin, assign a test user the "Time Clock" role.
2. Log out, log back in as that Time Clock user.
3. Open a Work Order that has a Digital Inspection and look at the inspection status labels.
Expected Result: Time Clock user has no Work Orders access, so cannot see inspections or their status labels.
Actual Result (Observed): Because the Time Clock role grants workOrdersView, the user reaches the WO and the inspection status labels ARE visible — contradicting "no access".
Reason for Failure (Root Cause): Same root cause as DI-111 — the live "Time Clock" role includes workOrdersView, so WO content (including inspection status labels) is visible. This is the same role-template drift, surfaced on the status-label check.
Severity: Medium (same underlying Time Clock role drift).
